items.title: Johor DAP voices full confidence in Anthony Loke, vows to regroup for next general election
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 3 — Johor DAP has expressed its full support for DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke to continue leading the party despite DAP and Pakatan Harapan (PH) suffering a setback in the Negeri Sembilan state election. Its chairman Teo Nie Ching said the decision was made at a Johor DAP committee meeting in Kulai this afternoon, which also discussed the Negeri Sembilan state election results and their implications for the party’s preparations for the next general election (GE). “Johor DAP respects the decision made by the people of Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Police seek KLIA CCTV in probe into Malaysia Airlines pilot accused of smuggling RM45m in ecstasy to Jakarta
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Malaysian police are investigating whether a drug syndicate used flight crews and air routes to smuggle narcotics after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was accused of transporting RM45 million worth of ecstasy into Indonesia. The Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department is seeking CCTV footage from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to establish how the alleged smuggling operation was carried out, Utusan Malaysia reported today. The department’s director, Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, said checks showed that the pilot had no previous criminal record with the Royal Malaysia Police.

items.title: #NSTviral: Motorcyclists running red light spark public anger on social media
items.summary: Several users criticised the motorcyclists' actions, saying such behaviour could put other road users at risk and burden emergency responders if an accident occurred. Another user questioned whether enforcement action would be taken against such road offences. user Lim Sg commented.

items.title: Kuantan student dies after motorcycle slams into stationary Triton on LPT2 returning from RXZ event
items.summary: The victim, Arissa Shazzira Zainudin, 21, from Kuantan, died after the motorcycle she was riding crashed into the rear of a four-wheel drive vehicle at KM356 of the East Coast Expressway 2 (LPT2), near Bukit Besi, at 4.55pm. Dungun district police chief Supt Nik Ab. Halim Nik Mat said the four-wheel drive vehicle had stopped in the emergency lane.

items.title: Malaysian alleged human-trafficking ringleader held in Thailand after ‘coffee money’ bribe attempt
items.summary: SONGKHLA, Aug 3 — A Malaysian believed to be one of the leaders of a transnational human trafficking syndicate has been arrested in southern Thailand after allegedly offering “coffee money” to Immigration officers to secure the release of three Chinese nationals without valid travel documents. Police said the pair arrived while officers were processing the arrests of the three Chinese nationals and two Thai men detained earlier during an operation on Asian Highway 2 in Tha Chang, Bang Klam district. Three Chinese nationals without valid travel documents were found inside.

items.title: DAP's Steven Sim dismisses Pas confidence of winning Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang DAP chief Steven Sim has dismissed Pas' confidence of winning Penang in the next election, describing the remarks as "arrogant". Responding to remarks by Pas information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari that the current political wave would also see the party capture Penang in the next general election, Sim said such statements reflected overconfidence. "Some people asked me, as DAP Penang chief, what my response is.

items.title: Melaka Opposition leader expects BN-Perikatan talks soon on state election pact
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 3 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) leaders are expected to hold talks soon over a possible electoral pact for the Melaka state election, state Opposition leader Mohd Yadzil Yaakub told national daily The Star . Mohd Yadzil said Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh and Parti Wawasan Negara president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin were likely to meet, although he declined to disclose how many seats his coalition expected to contest. “In my view, the Negeri Sembilan state election carried a message far greater than merely a change of state government.

items.title: Airline strike in Canada grounds estimated 250,000 passengers
items.summary: TRENTON: More than 4,000 flight attendants at WestJet, Canada's second-largest airline, went on strike Sunday, grounding about 600 daily flights and disrupting travel plans for an estimated 250,000 passengers, Anadolu Ajansi reported. Air Canada followed in February under a new contract. WestJet said affected passengers would receive refunds.

items.title: UK faces recession if Strait of Hormuz stays closed
items.summary: LONDON: Britain's economy is likely to shrink in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz does not reopen to shipping before the middle of next year, forecasters at accountants EY warned on Monday. EY slightly nudged up its growth forecast for this year to 0.8 per cent from 0.9 per cent, on the basis that the Strait reopens by the end of September, and sees growth of 1.2 per cent in 2027 on that basis. * EY predicts that if the Strait of Hormuz remains shut until early to mid 2027, UK growth this year will slow to 0.5 per cent and that the economy will shrink 0.2 per cent in 2027 * Inflation is likely to rise to 6.4 per cent by the end of 2026 under that scenario, compared with a lower peak of 3. per cent this year if the Strait reopens in the next couple of months * Bank of England forecasts last week, under an adverse scenario where oil and gas prices remain 30 per cent-60 per cent higher than markets expect, still showed the economy growing by close to 1.0 per cent next year while quarterly inflation peaked at 4.5 per cent * EY expects the BoE to keep interest rates on hold this year and then cut them next year from 3.75 per cent to 3.25 per cent with moves in April and July © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Gold gains as oil slumps after Trump holds off on Iran attack
items.summary: FUNDAMENTALS * Spot gold was up 0.7 per cent at US$4,067.06 per ounce, as of 0023 GMT. US gold futures rose 0.9 per cent to US$4,065.60. * Spot silver gained 0.7 per cent to US$58.02 per ounce, platinum climbed 0.7 per cent to US$1,653.78, and palladium firmed 1.5 per cent to US$1,293.00.

items.title: Chery to invest US$75mil in Korea's KG Mobility, eyes overseas markets
items.summary: SEOUL: China's Chery Automobile has agreed to invest US$75 million in South Korean automaker KG Mobility Corp through convertible bonds, KG Mobility said. "Chery has many manufacturing bases around the world. Chery is China's largest car exporter.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar ahead of key US economic data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Monday ahead of the release of key United States (US) economic data today amid easing tensions in Middle East. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) Manufacturing PMI for July will be released tonight, with the consensus estimate at 54.0, which is higher than June's reading of 53.3. Meanwhile, SPI Asset Management managing partner Stephen Innes said the US dollar weakened after Trump cancelled the planned strike on Iran over the weekend.

items.title: Oil tumbles as Trump cancels attack on Iran to reach nuclear deal
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Oil prices tumbled US$4 a barrel on Monday after US President Donald Trump held off on a fresh attack on Iran, seeking to reach a quick deal that would halt Tehran's nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures slid US$4.08, or 4.64 per cent, to US$83.85 by 2352 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$80.66 a barrel, down US$4.01, or 4.74 per cent. Both contracts jumped more than 20 per cent last month after fighting between the US and Iran resumed and as attacks on several tankers around Oman heightened security concerns, deterring shippers from entering the Gulf to load oil.

items.title: Peru probes crash of tourist plane that killed 13
items.summary: LIMA: Peruvian authorities said on Sunday they are investigating the crash of a small plane carrying tourists to view the famous Nazca Lines, which killed all 13 people on board. Once procedures at the crash site are completed, the investigation will be carried out "in coordination with the relevant authorities to determine the causes of this tragic plane crash", the Public Prosecutor's Office said in a statement. Early Sunday, Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni offered her "deepest condolences for the tragic plane crash in Peru, in which seven Italian citizens lost their lives".

items.title: Four Al-Fayed survivors told they were trafficking victims
items.summary: LONDON: Four women who allege abuse by late Harrods owner Mohamed Al-Fayed have been confirmed as victims of human trafficking by the UK's Interior Ministry, a group representing the survivors told AFP on Monday. Four women, who use the pseudonyms Isabella, Justine, Elizabeth and Margo and founded the "No One Above" advocacy group, have now been recognised as victims of human trafficking. Isabella, who worked in Fayed's Harrods office in 2001, said she was recognised as a trafficking victim in May.

items.title: Why Malaysia's regional economies remain weakly integrated
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is politically and administratively integrated, but its production economy remains considerably less integrated. A truly integrated economy is one in which firms across regions purchase inputs from one another, exchange technology, provide specialised services and participate in shared value chains. Growth in one state should generate investment, employment and demand elsewhere through supplier networks rather than remain confined within isolated industrial clusters.

items.title: The end of the command-and-control CEO
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The greatest test of a chief executive officer (CEO) is not whether an organisation succeeds because of them, but whether it can continue succeeding without them. For decades, a CEO's success was measured by familiar metrics—strategy, revenue growth, profitability, capital allocation and risk management. Rather than making every critical decision, the CEO designs an organisation that enables thousands of good decisions to be made every day.

items.title: Home-grown firms rewrite Malaysia's export story
items.summary: Malaysia External Trade Development Corp (Matrade) chairman Datuk Seri Reezal Merican Naina Merican said Malaysia's deep integration into global value chains has long created the perception that foreign multinationals are the main engines of export success. Total trade rose 22.4 per cent year-on-year to a record RM1.796 trillion, while exports climbed 27.5 per cent to RM971.59 billion, the fastest growth since 2021. The trade surplus surged 159.8 per cent to RM147.15 billion, equivalent to 94 per cent of the surplus recorded for the whole of 2025.

items.title: Ride-hailing, delivery demand holds despite cost squeeze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians are tightening their spending when using ride-hailing and food delivery services as rising living costs squeeze household budgets, prompting consumers to be more selective without significantly weakening demand, industry players said. Another 27 per cent said they would reduce their usage, while 17 per cent would only use the services when promotions are available. Masrizal said long-term growth requires a balance between consumers, platforms and drivers.

items.title: Growth wave demands bigger power supply
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will need to add substantial power generation capacity over the coming years as electricity demand accelerates, fuelled by investments in data centres, semiconductor manufacturing and other energy-intensive industries, according to Mitsubishi Power Asia-Pacific. "As demand continues to grow, Malaysia needs a significant addition to its power supply capacity," he said. He said the reservation agreements are intended to secure future equipment deliveries amid rising demand for power generation equipment globally.

items.title: Bar's appeal over Najib's reduced sentence among key court hearings this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Several court proceedings involving prominent political figures and major corruption cases are set to unfold in the coming week. On Friday, the Court of Appeal is expected to fix a date to deliver its judgment in the Malaysian Bar's appeal challenging the Pardons Board's decision to halve former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's prison sentence and reduce his fine in the SRC International case. A three-member panel chaired by Judge Lim Chong Fong had on July 31 reserved its decision in the appeal, which challenges the High Court's earlier refusal to grant leave for judicial review of the board's decision.

items.title: DAP warned against Cabinet exit after electoral setbacks [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Quitting the cabinet may help DAP rebuild credibility among its traditional supporters after successive electoral defeats, but the political cost would outweigh any benefits, said Dr Ong Kian Ming. The former Bangi member of parliament from DAP said this when asked about the party's options after Pakatan Harapan's loss in Saturday's Negri Sembilan election. DAP also lost the Repah seat.

items.title: Israeli strikes kill 13 in Gaza
items.summary: GAZA CITY: Israeli strikes on Gaza hit multiple residential buildings and killed at least 13 people, authorities said on Sunday, despite Hamas saying it had agreed to the latest stage of a deal to end the war. Gaza's civil defence rescue service, which operates under Hamas authority, said on Sunday that eight people were killed in strikes around midnight that hit multiple residential buildings, while five others were killed later in the day. In one overnight attack near the central Gaza Strip, a man and his wife were killed and several others were wounded when an Israeli military helicopter struck an apartment, a civil defence spokesman said.

items.title: Negri polls expose PH's struggle to win Malay support [WATCH]
items.summary: Umno secured 16 seats for BN, while MCA won two. Within PH, DAP scored nine victories, followed by PKR with two seats. "BN and PN combined their Malay support.

items.title: The Blue Wave's biggest test begins now
items.summary: THE outcome of the Negri Sembilan election on Aug 1 confirms that the "Blue Wave" has evolved from campaign rhetoric into a measurable electoral reality. The defeats of prominent PH leaders in Chennah and Linggi were symbols of a broader political shift. BN strengthened its position across Malay-majority, rural and semi-urban constituencies, while PH largely retained support in selected urban seats.

items.title: Hot mornings, rainy afternoons: Why Malaysia keeps getting thunderstorms despite the dry season
items.summary: According to Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip, neither assumption tells the full story. He said the recent run of afternoon thunderstorms was caused by temporary changes in wind patterns and the presence of higher levels of atmospheric moisture, rather than a shift in Malaysia’s seasonal weather. MetMalaysia director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the recent afternoon thunderstorms are temporary and were caused by shifting wind patterns and higher atmospheric moisture, rather than an unusual change in the Southwest Monsoon.

items.title: Protect yourself from lightning: MetMalaysia debunks dangerous thunderstorm myths
items.summary: Once thunder is heard or thick storm clouds begin forming, people are already in a lightning-risk area and should seek shelter immediately. — Bernama pic Dangerous assumptions Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said these assumptions continue to place people at unnecessary risk. “Once thick cumulonimbus clouds begin to form and thunder can be heard, people are already within an area at risk of being struck by lightning and should immediately seek shelter,” he said.

items.title: Iran says close to Hormuz deal with Oman after US suspends attack plan
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran on Sunday said it was nearing a deal with Oman over a new route through the Strait of Hormuz, hours after the US called off major strikes to allow for diplomacy. US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that his country and Israel had agreed to hold off on new strikes on Iran, saying the "perimeters" of a deal were there. The foes have been at war since February 28, when the US and Israel launched surprise strikes against Iran, although months of on-and-off diplomacy have led to periods of relative calm.

items.title: Trump says new Iran talks to begin Monday after calling off strikes
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said negotiations with Iran will begin on Monday after he decided to hold off on new "disastrous" strikes against the Islamic republic to pursue a deal. On Saturday, the US president pulled back from threats of a massive attack against Iran, which he said would have been the biggest since World War II, saying the "perimeter" of a deal was there. And the reason they ask is they think there's a deal," Trump said.

items.title: 2,000 take part in Sarawak Jom Heboh run
items.summary: KOTA SAMARAHAN: About 2,000 people took part in the Jom Heboh Fun Run here yesterday. As a light drizzle fell, Media Prima Omnia chief operating officer Datuk Mohd Efendi Omar flagged off the participants, comprising people all ages, including families, youths and health-conscious individuals. To accommodate participants with different fitness levels, the run featured two distance categories: 5km and 8km.

items.title: Trump says US support for Japanese yen a 'signal of friendship'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump on Sunday confirmed that the United States had intervened to support the Japanese yen, calling the move a "signal of friendship" that would financially benefit the US and the world economy. The Financial Times reported on Friday that the US Treasury had jointly intervened with Japan to prop up the yen for the first time in nearly three decades. Asked aboard Air Force One why the US was moving to support Japan's currency, Trump said: "Because we have a good relationship with Japan."

items.title: Sultan Nazrin joins Run for Tigers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah and Raja Permaisuri of Perak Tuanku Zara Salim yesterday joined more than 4,000 participants at the Run for Tigers: The Long Run, a flagship Global Tiger Day event promoting awareness and support for Malayan tiger conservation. Joining the royal couple were their children, Raja Kecil Besar of Perak Raja Azlan Muzaffar Shah and Raja Nazira Safya Shah. Organised by WWF-Malaysia and Maybank, the event also marked a decade of partnership between the organisations in supporting the critically endangered Malayan tiger.

items.title: HLIB Research starts coverage on MFM with 'buy' call
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research) has initiated coverage on Malayan Flour Mills Bhd (MFM) with a "buy" rating and a target price of 93 sen. The target price is based on seven times its mid-financial year 2027 core earnings per share (EPS) estimate of 13.3 sen. HLIB Research said MFM is expected to record a three-year compound annual growth rate of 7.5 per cent in core earnings for financial years 2026 to 2028. It said the earnings growth would be underpinned by improved operating efficiency at MFM's flour milling operations in Malaysia and Vietnam, as well as favourable input cost dynamics.

items.title: At least 72 die in Spain's Ceuta migrant rush
items.summary: CEUTA: At least 72 people died during the recent mass influx of migrants into Spain's Ceuta enclave from Morocco, Spanish officials said on Sunday, although Moroccan officials later presented a lower estimate. Most of the estimated 60,000 people who rushed into Spain's North African territory — most by swimming — have returned to Morocco since the territory's largest mass migrant crossing. Later on Sunday, Morocco's Interior Ministry issued its own toll, saying 11 people had died trying to reach Ceuta.

items.title: S. Korea temperature hits record high of 42.5°C
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea yesterday registered its highest temperature since records began more than a century ago, according to the state weather agency. Yangsan has been the epicentre of the ongoing heatwave, where the mercury exceeded 40°C for a fifth consecutive day yesterday. More than 20 localities were under emergency heatwave alerts yesterday, a new warning category introduced this year to better address rising temperatures.

items.title: Japan quake leaves scars beyond the rubble
items.summary: HIROSUKE Shimada's home emerged largely unscathed from last week's earthquake in southwestern Japan, but the violent shaking left him, his wife and their three daughters too frightened to sleep inside, forcing them to live in a tent in the front yard. Across town, carpenter Makoto Sawatari surveyed crumbling plaster, smashed roof tiles and cracked windows, wondering how much it would cost to rebuild his home in the coastal city of Yatsushiro, a decade after another major earthquake damaged it. "The house is all right, but I'm still too scared to stay inside," his wife Yuka said, resting inside the tent.

items.title: OPEC+ boosts September oil output by 188,000 barrels a day
items.summary: LONDON: Saudi Arabia, Russia and five other key members of OPEC+ agreed in an online meeting Sunday to boost oil production by 188,000 barrels a day from September, against a backdrop of disruption caused by the Middle East war. "The seven participating countries decided to implement a production adjustment of 188 thousand barrels per day," they said in a joint statement. The increase, decided by the key countries in the enlarged Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, was widely expected by analysts.

items.title: Hybrid Workday policy modernises Malaysia’s public sector as civil servants embrace digitalisation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — The implementation of the Hybrid Workday (HBH) Policy, which begins today for states observing a Friday-Saturday weekend, has been described as a positive step towards modernising and strengthening the digitalisation of public services without compromising service delivery to the people. In TERENGGANU, State Information Department information officer Izamuddin Jusoh @ Md Rahim, 37, said HBH supports the Public Service Department’s (JPA) digitalisation plan and does not affect productivity, thanks to effective monitoring by department heads. “My scope of work is flexible and mobile.

items.title: Show evidence suspects fled to Malaysia, Kelantan police tell Thai authorities amid 90km border fence plan
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 2 — The Kelantan police have requested the Thai authorities to provide any information or evidence if it is true that the suspects involved in the shooting incident that recently claimed the lives of five of their (Thai) security personnel have fled to Malaysia. Its police chief, Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said that so far they have not received any intelligence information confirming the allegation, and monitoring by the Special Branch of the Kelantan police contingent headquarters (IPK), and all district police headquarters in the state have not detected any movement of the suspects entering Malaysia. He said that with enhanced control, the allegation that crime suspects can easily escape to Malaysia should no longer arise.

items.title: BN thanks Tuanku Muhriz for consenting to Ismail Lasim’s appointment as Negeri Sembilan MB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has expressed its gratitude to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, for consenting to the appointment of Datuk Ismail Lasim as the state’s new Menteri Besar. BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the coalition also expressed its gratitude for Tuanku Muhriz’s consent to the formation of the Negeri Sembilan state government through the cooperation between BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN). Earlier, Ismail, who is also the Juasseh state assemblyman, was sworn in as the Menteri Besar of Negeri Sembilan before Tuanku Muhriz during a ceremony held at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Police arrest seven, including two teens, in Jalan Ampang knife‑point robbery investigation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Police arrested seven individuals, including two teenage girls, to assist in the investigation of a knife-point robbery case at a residential unit in Jalan Ampang last Friday. Wangsa Maju district police chief ACP Annas Sulaiman said that the police arrested five men aged 22 to 38 and and two teenage girls aged 13 and 19 in the parking area in Jalan Metro Pudu here at 3 am yesterday. Members of the public who have information related to the incident are requested to contact the District Control Centre of the Wangsa Maju district police headquarters at 03-9289 9222, the Kuala Lumpur police Hotline at 03-2115 9999 or any nearby police station.

items.title: Thunderstorm warning issued for 10 states until 6pm
items.summary: In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected areas are Perlis; Kedah involving Padang Terap, Kuala Muda, Sik, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu; and Perak covering Kerian, Larut, Matang and Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim The warning also covers Kelantan (Pasir Mas, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Gua Musang), the whole of Terengganu, and several areas in Pahang, namely Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Jerantut, Bentong, Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin. In Selangor, only Hulu Selangor is affected, while in Johor, the areas involved are Batu Pahat, Kluang, Mersing, Pontian, Kulai, Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru. For Sarawak, the affected areas include Kuching (Bau and Kuching), Betong (Saratok and Kabong), Sarikei, Sibu (Sibu and Selangau), Mukah, Bintulu, Miri (Subis, Beluru, Miri and Marudi), and Limbang.

items.title: Fire breaks out at Sunway Square Mall, blaze contained before firefighters arrive (VIDEO)
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Aug 2 — A small kitchen fire at a restaurant in Sunway Square Mall was extinguished even before firefighters reached the scene early this morning, according to the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department. According to the New Straits Times , the department received an emergency call at 1.23am and dispatched a team from the Subang Jaya station. Eight personnel, a fire engine and a water tanker were deployed.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB: New state government committed to upholding royal institution
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today pledged that the state government would continue to uphold the royal institution and preserve the state’s customs and traditions as fundamental pillars of its administration. He said safeguarding the royal institution was the responsibility of every Negeri Sembilan citizen and remained essential to maintaining harmony and close relations between the monarchy and the state administration. Meanwhile, Ismail said the state government would continue strengthening cooperation with the Federal Government to ensure the interests and well-being of the people of Negeri Sembilan remained a priority.

items.title: Open to negotiations: Melaka MB says willing to discuss cooperation with any party for the coming state polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 2 — Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN) is open to cooperating with any party under a BN Plus formula for the upcoming state election, its chairman and Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said. Ab Rauf, who is also Melaka Umno liaison committee chairman, said the party welcomed discussions with any political party interested in working together for the state polls. The election saw BN win 18 state seats, PH 11 and PN seven, enabling BN and PN to form the Negeri Sembilan state government.

items.title: Gesture of appreciation: Negeri Sembilan MB announces special state public holiday tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — Newly sworn-in Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today announced a special public holiday for the state tomorrow, saying it is meant to recognise the efforts of those involved in the recently concluded state election. Speaking at his first press conference after taking his oath of office, Ismail said the holiday had received the consent of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. “His Royal Highness has also graciously consented for me to announce a special public holiday tomorrow for the people of Negeri Sembilan,” he said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan exco lineup to be discussed with Zahid, finalised by Friday, says new MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — Newly sworn-in Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said today that the composition of the state executive council (exco) will be discussed with Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi before a final decision is made, with appointments expected by Friday. Speaking to reporters after taking his oath of office, Ismail said he would also seek the views of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan before the lineup is finalised. Mohd Zuhaimi and Mohd Aidil secured 506 votes and 2,816 votes, respectively.

items.title: Police probe viral Pandamaran car park brawl involving 16-year-old student
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 2 — Police are investigating a viral video on social media showing a brawl at the Pandamaran Sports Complex car park in Klang last Friday. Klang Selatan police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the incident occurred at approximately 1.20pm involving two men, one of whom is a 16-year-old student. Lim urged anyone with information on the incident to come forward and contact the investigating officer, Insp Mohammad Baaz Mohd Zohari, at 016-4117885, the Klang Selatan IPD operations room at 03-3376 2222, or any nearby police station.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz tells Negeri Sembilan assemblymen to put people above politics
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, today reminded members of the State Legislative Assembly to always place the interests of the state and its people above political or personal considerations in carrying out the mandate entrusted to them. His Royal Highness said every elected representative bears a significant responsibility, as they are entrusted with bringing the voices, aspirations, needs, and concerns of the people to the State Legislative Assembly. Tuanku Muhriz stressed that every policy, plan, and decision made should reflect those aspirations and remain firmly focused on the welfare of the people and the continued development of Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: BN will deliver responsible and people-centred govt in Negeri Sembilan, says Zambry
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — Barisan Nasional (BN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the mandate entrusted to the coalition by voters in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election would be translated into a responsible, people-centred administration anchored on stability, integrity, and the state’s continued development. Zambry also thanked party members, campaign workers, election machinery, volunteers, and supporters whose dedication contributed to BN’s performance in the state election. The Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly was dissolved on June 5 after the state BN withdrew its support for the leadership of Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun on April 27, triggering the state election For the latest news on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Who is Ismail Lasim, the new Negeri Sembilan menteri besar?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Datuk Ismail Lasim has been officially sworn in as the new menteri besar of Negeri Sembilan before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. The ceremony marks a major transition in the state’s leadership, elevating a veteran politician and legal practitioner to the top executive office after more than two decades of public service in state administration. Ismail’s rise to the state’s highest political office comes as a continuation of his long-standing presence in Negeri Sembilan politics.

items.title: It’s official: Ismail Lasim takes over as Negeri Sembilan menteri besar
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — Juasseh State Assemblyman Datuk Ismail Lasim was today sworn in as the new Menteri Besar of Negeri Sembilan. Barisan Nasional (BN) deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and other state elected representatives were also present. In the 15th Negeri Sembilan state election, PH won 17 state seats, followed by BN (14) and PN (five), leading to the formation of a PH-BN state government.

items.title: Ismail Lasim among three tipped for Negeri Sembilan menteri besar post
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 2 — Kuala Pilah Umno chief Datuk Ismail Lasim is among three candidates tipped to be appointed as Negeri Sembilan’s new Menteri Besar. Ismail, 67, who is also a member of the Umno Supreme Council, won the Juasseh state seat in yesterday’s 16th Negeri Sembilan state election. The two other names being floated are Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, 62, the Negeri Sembilan Umno liaison chairman and Jelebu MP who retained the Pertang state seat, and Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, 47, the former state deputy speaker who won the Lenggeng seat.

items.title: Selangor Veterinary Department probes viral dog abuse incident in Port Klang
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 2 — The Selangor Department of Veterinary Services (JPV Selangor) has launched a criminal investigation after a video showing a group of individuals restraining and dragging a dog by its neck went viral, culminating in the animal’s death. According to the department, multiple complaints were lodged through the MyAnimalWelfare system at around 9.25pm on 30 July 2026 after the video began circulating online. On 31 July, at about 11am, JPV Selangor’s Animal Welfare Team received the carcass of a male dog — believed to be the same animal seen in the video — along with an orange icebox from a local woman who surrendered the remains.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan to swear In new menteri besar this morning, chosen candidate still unknown
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 2 — Negeri Sembilan will install its new menteri besar this morning, with the swearing‑in ceremony scheduled to take place at the Balairung Seri, Istana Besar Seri Menanti at 10.15am, according to a media notice shared via WhatsApp. Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said he submitted three names to the Yang di‑Pertuan Besar during an audience at Istana Hinggap last night, stressing that the choice rests entirely with the ruler. The swearing‑in follows the outcome of the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, where BN won 18 seats, Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured 11, and Perikatan Nasional (PN) took seven.

items.title: Man drowns after saving eight-year-old great-nephew from Terengganu river
items.summary: Hulu Terengganu police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said firefighters recovered the body of Harun Ibrahim from the riverbank at about 7.30 pm, about 100 metres from the spot where he was reported missing. “The victim was eventually found on the riverbank by the Malaysia Fire and Rescue Department’s Water Rescue Team after the water level dropped during the search and rescue operation. Police advise the public to remain vigilant and exercise caution when visiting water recreation areas, given the recent spell of unpredictable weather,” he said.

items.title: After viral video shows young girl being molested, Sungai Buloh police searching for perpetrator
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Police are tracking down a foreign man suspected of molesting an 11-year-old girl at a business premises in Sungai Buloh, Selangor, on Wednesday (July 29). Sungai Buloh police chief Supt Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said they received a report from the Kampung Baru Subang police station regarding the incident. He urged those with information regarding the case to contact the investigation officer, Insp Muhammad Amirul Amin Shukor, at 013-6695290 or the nearest police station.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan state election sees 30 candidates losing their deposits
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — A total of 30 candidates lost their deposits after failing to garner at least one-eighth of the total of votes counted in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election. Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), which did not win a single seat and failed to defend its Labu seat, suffered the biggest loss, with 23 out of 24 of its candidates losing their deposits. Also, the sole candidate from Parti Orang Asli Malaysia (ASLI) and Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM) both lost their deposit, along with one Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate, and four independent candidates.

items.title: Out of nine women candidates in Negeri Sembilan polls, only three winners
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 2 — Only three of nine women candidates who contested in the Negeri Sembilan state election prevailed over their opponents, according to the Election Commission’s (EC) official results. S Leza (6,830 votes) won by a majority of 730 votes against PH candidate Datuk Noorzunita Begum (6,100 votes), while Siti Nur Umaira (14,209 votes) won by a majority of 5,279 votes against PH candidate Ahmad Faez Abdul Razak (8,930 votes) and Bersatu’s Mohamad Hanifah Abu Baker (1,985 votes). Meanwhile, Nicole Tan defended her Bukit Kepayang seat with a majority of 15,207 votes by polling 24,096 votes against PN’s Lee Boon Shian, who garnered 8,889 votes.

items.title: Both youngest and oldest winning Negeri Sembilan state election winners from Umno
items.summary: Siti Nur Umaira, the Rasah Umno Puteri division chief, secured 14,209 votes to win the seat with a majority of 5,279 votes, defeating Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Ahmad Faez Abdul Razak (8,930 votes) and Bersatu incumbent Mohamad Hanifah Abu Baker (1,985 votes). Meanwhile, Mohamad retained the Rantau state seat by securing 19,050 votes to defeat PH’s Dr Azizul Hakim Mahdi (7,032 votes) in a straight fight. He polled 32,004 votes in a three-cornered fight, defeating PH’s Ahmad Shahir Mohd Shah (15,045 votes) and Bersatu’s Mohd Nazree Mohd Yunus (2,205 votes).
